question.problem:
For the twice-differentiable function $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R,$ we have the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,0,0) & =-1, & \,{f}^{′}(1,0,0) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(1,0,0) & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Use the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14197045/assets/31305b4a4a27141bae70eabbb04acaf98928c275f8efec37ef8a869c7599a2f3.svg) to approximate the value of $f(1,1,1).$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that the function $\mathbf{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14197045/assets/a7a5f8961c77ad8a606ce57a543d5606b834061f3a0777b074a5711dcc9a4529.svg) 

and is twice differentiable at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a.$ Then, the quadratic Taylor polynomial of $f$ about $\mathbf a$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{1}{2}(x-a)^{T}{f}^{″}(a)(x-a),\end{aligned}
$$

where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14197045/assets/276fd591c58ea0bd80eb0d3c236ade53fcd1d38864ccd650873cf052561b7586.svg)

and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14197045/assets/06c98e6248f7fdb303c04772921b0423f8e2f88450d330c295bc3a72846ef858.svg)

In this case, we have ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14197045/assets/3ac30d1603a502de1404a1888f7c410d22ae93b8b47db6694734a09634a43954.svg) and the following data:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(a) & =-1, & \,{f}^{′}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}], & \,{f}^{″}(a) & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the second-degree Taylor polynomial is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14197045/assets/afd14fa251e88edb40ea71b70c56db5a03ec83d906608930e2b3ba3ba9c9fb0b.svg)

Finally, evaluating the polynomial at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14197045/assets/1af733b173aa4a358cd8c0b5c2754431be57887e7c43b0aa98125deefdecc4ad.svg) we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,1,1) & ≈-1+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}1-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-1+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-1+1+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
